comments.author: @hb1338
comments.text:
Sint Maarten is not particularly dangerous, though it would be improved by the installation of an ILS system. There is *never* any need for anybody to get anywhere near the exhaust of any departing or arriving aircraft - anybody who does so is downright stupid.
Campo de Marte (Congonhas) has a short runway, so it is used only for small aircraft operating domestic services - that does not make it dangerous. Aquaplaning Is no longer a concern, because the runway has been grooved in order to allow water to drain rapidly from the surface.
Gibraltar has had road tunnels under the runway since 2023.
Madeira is bumpy, and rarely pleasant to approach and land, but it is not particularly dangerous.
Barra airport is not dangerous - you overstate grossly the level of difficulty and danger. Departures and arrivals are scheduled so that any effect of the tides is minimal, and the airport is not licensed for night operations, which would only ever be used in an emergency.
